optimizedCVData.summary: Backend engineer with 11 years of experience designing and operating high-throughput services in Java, Kotlin and Python, including a settlement platform processing about 40 million events a day on Kafka. Reduced p99 latency of a payment status API from 480 ms to 120 ms by moving hot reads from PostgreSQL to Redis, and led a team of four through a nine-month monolith-to-microservices migration. After a planned career break for family caregiving, returned to active engineering with an AWS Solutions Architect Associate certification earned in 2024 and continued open-source contributions in Kotlin. Brings deep experience in event-driven architecture, API design and scalable backend systems, with a track record of cross-functional ownership from design through on-call production support.

bullets: Maintained backend engineering skills during full-time family caregiving by completing an AWS Solutions Architect Associate preparation course and earning the certification in 2024.
Participated in a reading group working through Designing Data-Intensive Applications, reinforcing knowledge of distributed systems, database internals and scalable architecture patterns.
Contributed bug fixes to an open-source Kotlin library, keeping hands-on with the language and the pull-request review cycle.
Designed and operated the settlement service in Kotlin and Spring Boot, handling about 40 million events a day on Kafka with consistent sub-second processing.
Cut p99 latency of the payment status API from 480 ms to 120 ms by moving hot reads from PostgreSQL to Redis, eliminating database contention under peak load.
Led a team of 4 engineers through a nine-month migration from a monolith to 6 independent services, coordinating API contracts, data ownership boundaries and phased cutover.
Served as on-call engineer for the payments platform and authored post-incident reviews for 14 incidents, driving systemic fixes that reduced repeat pages.
Built order and inventory services in Java and Spring, backed by PostgreSQL for persistence and RabbitMQ for asynchronous event processing.
Introduced consumer-driven contract tests that reduced integration bugs found in staging by about a third, shortening the feedback loop between services.
Contributed to API design reviews and code review processes across the backend team, establishing shared standards for service interfaces.
Delivered internal web tools for two clients using Java and JavaScript, covering requirements gathering, backend implementation and handoff to client teams.

coverLetter:
Priya Raman
Toronto, Canada
priya.raman@example.com
+1 555 0176

October 12, 2026

Hiring Manager
Duolingo

Dear Hiring Manager,

Scaling a backend service to handle tens of millions of events a day sounds straightforward until the latency spikes and the on-call queue fills up. At Lumen Payments, I faced that problem directly: our payment status API was too slow under load, so I moved hot reads from PostgreSQL to Redis and brought p99 latency down from 480 ms to 120 ms. That kind of diagnosis-first, fix-second thinking is exactly what Duolingo's backend teams need when running hundreds of simultaneous experiments across half a billion learners.

As a Senior Backend Engineer with eleven years building payment and event-processing systems in Kotlin, Java and Python, I've worked across the full lifecycle that this role describes: designing services, shipping them to production and owning them on call. At Lumen, I also led a four-engineer team through a nine-month migration from a monolith to six independent services, which required the same cross-functional coordination and milestone ownership your job description calls out. My observability work has been done in Datadog, and my cloud experience is on AWS, where I hold a current Solutions Architect Associate certification.

I'd welcome the chance to talk through how my background maps to the specific team you're hiring for. I'm available for an interview at your convenience.

Best regards,
Priya Raman
